quandoUsar: Inspecting API responses, webhook events, or log records in internal tools and debugging panels.
When the user needs to find a key or value in a large object: search highlights the matches and opens the branches that contain them.
When a field's path matters: the current row shows its own (`order.items[0].sku`) and offers actions to copy the value or the path.
quandoEvitar: Use `code-block` to show a short JSON snippet as static code.
Use `tree-view` to navigate a hierarchy of items with their own labels; here each row is always a key and a value.
Use `sortable-data-table` when the JSON is a list of records with the same fields, which compare better in columns.

teclado.acao: Move the current row; `Home` and `End` go to the first and last.
`→` opens the branch or, if already open, goes to the first child; `←` closes the branch or goes back to the parent.
Open or close the branch; on the “Show N more” row, load the next page.
Moves focus to the search field.
In the search field, go to the next and previous match; `Esc` clears the search and `↓` returns to the tree.
Trigger copying the focused row's value; with `Shift`, its path.

acessibilidade: Follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: `role="tree"` named by `label` and `treeitem` rows with level, position, `aria-expanded`, and an `aria-label` that summarizes key, type, and value; only the current row is in the `Tab` order.
The search match count is `aria-live`, and the result of each copy (success or failure) is announced in a `role="status"` region.
The row copy buttons are outside the `Tab` order (by keyboard, use the shortcut) and the one on the path bar is focusable; the interface texts are hardcoded in English.
movimento: When opening or closing a branch, loading a page, or expanding everything, each row unfolds its own height on a spring with no overshoot, with a fade.
The current row's highlight slides from one row to another, and the scrolling that keeps that row in view (or centers a search match) uses the same spring.
With “reduced motion”, rows, highlight, and scrolling change instantly; above 400 visible rows, row animation is turned off for everyone.
responsivo: The tree scrolls internally, limited by `maxHeight` (420 px by default); rows don't wrap, long values are truncated with an ellipsis, and strings over 40 characters show the full text in the `title`.
On screens up to 420 px the per-level indent drops from 16 px to 12 px, keys take at most 40% of the row, and the type disappears from the path bar.
desempenho: Long arrays and objects enter in pages of `pageSize` (50 by default) with a “Show N more” row; there is no virtualization, so each visible row is an element.
Search scans the entire JSON on every keystroke and stops at 2,000 matches; with very large payloads, typing can lag.
notasIA: Pass the already-parsed value (object or array) in `data`, not the JSON text: a string would appear as a single value.

Paths start from `rootName` (default `root`), like `root.users[0].name`: this is the format that `expanded`, `defaultExpanded`, `onSelect`, and `onCopy` use, and `defaultExpandDepth` opens the first levels.

It already comes with its own border, background, and scrolling (`maxHeight`), so it doesn't need another card around it; `searchable`, `copyable`, and `showPath` turn off search, copy, and the path bar.
